comment_box:
The Washington State Coalition Against Domestic Violence (WSCADV) writes to express our strong opposition to the Department of Veterans Affairs’ Proposed Rule on Reproductive Health Services. We also write in full support of the public comment submitted by the National Alliance to End Sexual Violence (NAESV) and the 25 undersigned national and state organizations.

As Washington State’s leading voice advocating for survivors of domestic violence and sexual assault, WSCADV is deeply concerned that the Proposed Rule would roll back critical reproductive healthcare access for veterans and their families—particularly those who have experienced sexual and domestic violence. The VA’s proposal to reinstate pre-2022 exclusions on abortion and abortion counseling would deny essential care to survivors, including in cases of rape, incest, or threats to the life or health of the pregnant person.

Veterans in Washington State and across the country deserve access to comprehensive, trauma-informed healthcare. This includes reproductive healthcare that recognizes the unique needs of survivors of military sexual trauma (MST), intimate partner violence, and other forms of gender-based violence. The VA’s own data and national research have consistently shown that women veterans experience sexual violence at disproportionately high rates, and that MST is associated with serious long-term health consequences including PTSD, depression, and substance use disorders.

Restricting access to abortion and abortion counseling not only undermines bodily autonomy—it also increases the risk of continued abuse and trauma. Survivors must be empowered to make decisions about their own health and futures, especially when those decisions are shaped by experiences of violence. The VA’s healthcare system must be a place of safety, healing, and support—not one that retraumatizes survivors by denying them care.

We urge the Department to reject the Proposed Rule and maintain the protections established in the 2022 Interim Final Rule and the 2024 Final Rule. WSCADV stands with NAESV and other advocates in calling for the VA to uphold its commitment to the health and dignity of all veterans and their families.
